title: Retention-matched 28 kT magnetic tunnel junction for DRAM duty
idea: Derive the barrier from the job: DRAM data must survive ~1 s, so Delta = ln(1 s / 1 ns) ~ 21 kT plus array/ECC margin ~ 28 kT at 85 C, not the 60 kT used for NVM. Shrink a perpendicular CoFeB/MgO free layer to ~8 nm at Delta ~ 28 kT and add a background read-scrub that rewrites only ECC-flagged flips every ~100 ms.
why: STT write current scales with Delta, so write energy (~30 fJ) and junction size both drop ~2x versus NVM-grade MRAM. There is no capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and no leakage refresh (fact 3), and the cell can reach 4F2 cross-point density.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer bit with zero bond-breaking switching
idea: Use rhombohedral-stacked bilayer hBN or MoS2: its out-of-plane polarization flips when one layer slides by a/sqrt(3), so the barrier is only interlayer stacking energy (meV per cell, ~1 eV for a 10 nm domain) and no ion or bond moves. Read the polarization non-destructively through the field it imposes on an adjacent MoS2 channel.
why: Fatigue mechanisms (vacancy migration, domain pinning) need bond rearrangement; removing them targets >1e12 endurance at ~aJ switching energy in an atomically thin cell. Attacks the charge wall (1), destructive read (8) and voltage floor (10).

title: Pre-buckled 2D membrane snap-through as a leak-free mechanical bit
idea: Clamp a 20 nm MoS2 or graphene drum under compressive prestrain so it has two buckled states separated by an elastic barrier of ~1 eV (~40 kT). A ~1 V electrostatic pulse snaps it through in ~1/f0 ~ 1 ns, and a local sense transistor reads up/down as a ~10 aF capacitance change.
why: A mechanical position has no leakage path, so retention is set by the elastic barrier, not a 13 fA tail, and refresh (fact 3) disappears. There is no storage capacitor (fact 1), and write energy is ~CV2 ~ 10 aJ.

title: Single-proton tautomer molecules as one-nanometer dipole bits
idea: Self-assemble a monolayer of porphycene-type molecules whose inner hydrogen pair hops between two nitrogen sites, with substituents tuning the proton double-well barrier to ~0.8 eV for >=1 s retention. A gate pulse flips the ~100 tautomers under a 10x10 nm electrode, and their collective dipole shifts the threshold of a 2D-channel read transistor.
why: From first principles, the smallest object with a room-temperature-grade barrier is one proton in a double well (~1 nm3). Storage density is then limited only by addressing, at aJ switching energy, with no capacitor (fact 1) or charge leakage (fact 3).

title: Geiger-mode avalanche read of a hundred-electron storage node
idea: Shrink the storage node to ~20 aF holding ~100 electrons and wire it as the bias of a SPAD-like junction. At read the junction is armed above breakdown for ~2 ns: a stored '1' tips it into avalanche (gain ~1e5) and a '0' does not, then an active quench resets it.
why: Poisson statistics need only N >= 36 electrons for 6-sigma discrimination, and kT/C noise on 20 aF is ~2 electrons rms. Storing 31,000 electrons is an artifact of bitline charge sharing, so the capacitor shrinks ~50x, deleting the 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1) and 1-2 patterning layers (fact 4).

title: Sub-damage-threshold direct-tunneling charge trap with volatile retention
idea: Store ~500 electrons in a nitride layer whose traps are engineered ~0.9 eV deep behind a 1.6 nm SiO2 tunnel oxide, written by direct tunneling at <2 V. Electrons never exceed the ~2-3 eV hot-carrier energy that generates oxide defects, and thermal emission gives ~0.5 s retention at 85 C (~100 s at 25 C), matched to refresh.
why: Flash wear-out is hot-carrier defect generation, so staying below that energy aims at >1e15 cycles. Gives a capacitorless ~4F2 1T cell with no pillar (facts 1, 4).

title: Landau-stabilized negative-capacitance boost layer inside storage capacitor
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric layer in series with the ZrO2-based dielectric and match the capacitances so the ferroelectric sits in its hysteresis-free negative-dC/dV Landau region. The series capacitance is then C_eff = C_d*|C_fe|/(|C_fe| - C_d), 3-5x above the dielectric alone.
why: Delivers the effective 'k ~ 70' that fact 1 calls for without new high-k chemistry, cutting capacitor aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~20:1 with large etch and deposition capital savings.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops storing single flux quanta at 4 K
idea: Store each bit as the presence or absence of one flux quantum (Phi0 = 2.07e-15 Wb) in a loop of 20 nm NbN nanowire. Huge kinetic inductance keeps beta_L = 2*pi*L*Ic/Phi0 > 1 in a ~100 nm loop, the persistent current never decays, and a nanocryotron reads it.
why: Zero leakage and write energy ~Ic*Phi0 ~ 1e-19 J, ~1000x below DRAM. Aimed at cryogenic AI and quantum-control racks; density is set by loop inductance, not capacitor charge (facts 1, 3, 10).

title: Stray-field-free antiferromagnetic tunnel junction bits packed at pitch
idea: Build Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions, where cluster-octupole order gives TMR with no net moment, and write them by spin-orbit torque with ps-scale intrinsic dynamics. With zero stray field, neighbor cells sit at 1-2F spacing without dipolar disturb.
why: Ferromagnetic MRAM density is capped by stray-field coupling; antiferromagnetic order removes it. Aims at sub-ns write and near-4F2 density with no capacitor or refresh (facts 1, 3).

title: Magnetoelectric exchange-coupled write: attojoule polarization flips magnet
idea: Put a 20 nm La-doped BiFeO3 layer under a CoFe nanomagnet: a ~100-200 mV pulse rotates BFO's coupled ferroelectric/antiferromagnetic order, and interfacial exchange drags the magnet 180 degrees. An MTJ on top reads the state.
why: Write energy is ~2Pr*A*V ~ 1e-16 J for a 30 nm cell at 0.1 V, ~1000x below current-driven STT and well under the CV2 floor of fact 10.

title: Polar flux-closure vortex chirality as a sub-5 nm ferroelectric bit
idea: In PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice nanodots, polarization curls into closed vortices that carry no surface bound charge, so the depolarizing field vanishes. Store the bit as vortex chirality (clockwise or counterclockwise), written by a curled field from an offset electrode pair and read through the chiral piezo or tunneling signal.
why: Ordinary ferroelectric bits fail below ~10 nm because depolarization energy beats the barrier; closure textures delete that term. Aims at a 3-5 nm polar bit (density) with no charge leakage (fact 3).

title: Atomically precise one-nanometer gold clusters as room-temperature Coulomb-blockade bits
idea: Derive the island from e2/2C >= 25 kT at 300 K: C <= 0.12 aF, a sub-1 nm island, which lithography cannot make but chemistry can (Au25(SR)18 clusters, ~1 eV charging gaps). Trap one cluster per cell between multiple tunnel junctions, store 0/1/2 electrons, and read with a single-electron-transistor electrometer, using the Coulomb staircase for 2 bits per cell.
why: Bits held as countable electrons need ~1 electron, not 31,000. Targets ~1e4x less stored charge, sub-aJ writes and multi-level density (facts 1, 10).

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor channel that stores and reads its own bit
idea: Use alpha-In2Se3, whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization sets its own band bending and conductance, as the transistor channel. A gate pulse writes the polarization, and the read is a non-destructive channel conductance with no separate capacitor or ferroelectric gate stack.
why: Storage and gain merge in one 2D layer, removing the capacitor (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8). Enables a vertical 4F2 cell with no capacitor etch.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM: freeze out leakage, then shrink the capacitor
idea: Run the array at 77 K, where thermally activated leakage (junction generation, subthreshold, trap-assisted) falls by >1e6 because it scales as exp(-Ea/kT). Design out the weakly temperature-dependent GIDL with a lower wordline-off bias, so a 0.3 fF planar MIM holds data for hours and refresh is dropped. Racks are LN2-cooled at ~10x wall-power overhead on the much smaller memory heat.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor charge wall (fact 1). Planar caps can approach 4F2 with no pillar etch, and bitline resistance falls ~5x.

title: Erasable conducting domain walls as non-destructive ferroelectric bits
idea: In thin-film z-cut LiNbO3-on-insulator, a field pulse injects a charged head-to-head domain wall between two electrodes that conducts ~uA, and a reverse pulse erases it. The read senses the wall current and never switches the polarization.
why: Read current is uA rather than fC, so reads are fast and non-destructive (fact 8). Walls are nanometers wide, so density is not capacitor-limited (fact 1), and nothing leaks (fact 3).

title: Charge-density-wave metastable state switched by picosecond electrical pulses
idea: Use the collective electron order of thin 1T-TaS2: a ~ps current pulse switches a nanoscale region from the insulating commensurate CDW into a metastable metallic 'hidden' state with 10-100x lower resistance. Confinement and strain engineering stretch its lifetime toward >=1 s at operating temperature.
why: The barrier is a collective electronic order (many electrons per nm3), giving ~fJ, ps switching with a non-destructive resistive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings replacing per-bit access transistors
idea: Store bits as charge packets in potential wells under 64 stacked gate electrodes along one vertical channel, reviving 1970s CCD memory in 3D. Packets clock to an end-of-string sense amp at ~1 ns per transfer with CTE >0.99999, and a page cache hides the shift latency.
why: With no capacitor and no access transistor per bit, both 3D-DRAM blockers (fact 2) vanish. One sense node serves 64 bits, cutting periphery share (fact 7), and each bit costs one deposited gate layer.

title: Expiring memory: retention sized to the data's lifetime, never refreshed
idea: AI activations, KV-cache blocks and gradients live 1-500 ms. The allocator tags each buffer with its lifetime and places it in banks whose measured cell retention exceeds that lifetime, and those banks never refresh because the data is dead before it decays.
why: Removes refresh energy and the 10-20% bandwidth loss (fact 3) for most AI traffic. Cells that only need ~100 ms retention can also use smaller capacitors (fact 1).

title: JEDEC 'one-second class' standard unlocking low-barrier memory elements
idea: Standardize a memory class with 1 s retention at 85 C, >=1e16 endurance and mandatory on-die ECC scrub. Barrier height = ln(retention/attempt time) kT, so emerging elements (MRAM, FeRAM, ReRAM) can be designed at ~28 kT instead of 60 kT, trading unneeded retention for write energy and endurance.
why: Write energy and wear scale with barrier height, so halving it gives new storage physics a qualified path to fill DRAM sockets now, raising usable supply.

title: Nanomechanical parametron storing the bit as oscillation phase
idea: Pump a ~1 um GHz nanomechanical or contour-mode AlN resonator at 2*f0 so it oscillates in one of two degenerate phases, 0 or pi. Write by briefly injecting a small f0 signal of the chosen phase, read by homodyne phase detection, and share one pump line across many frequency-multiplexed resonators.
why: The symmetry-broken phase ignores amplitude noise and has no charge-leakage tail (fact 3). Density is weaker, which suits radiation-hard or cryogenic niches.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode pair latch giving a static one-transistor cell
idea: Stack two heterojunction interband tunnel diodes in series (a Goto pair) on the storage node. Their N-shaped I-V gives two stable node voltages held only by the valley current; at ~1 A/cm2 valley density a 20 nm diode idles at ~4 pA, behind a single access transistor.
why: Static storage with no refresh (fact 3) in a 1T footprint and no capacitor pillar (fact 1). Needs peak/valley ratios well beyond today's silicon, hence the high risk.

title: Adiabatic ramped write that recovers the cell's CV2 energy
idea: A step charge through any resistor dissipates CV2/2, but a ramp of duration T >> RC dissipates only ~(RC/T)*CV2. Drive wordlines, bitlines and precharge from a resonant LC tank clock so cell writes ride a slow sinusoid and their charge returns to the tank.
why: Cuts write and precharge energy 3-10x at the same 1 V / 3 V levels, getting under the voltage floor (fact 10) without lowering voltage.

title: vdW-latched nanoparticle shuttle bit in a sealed nanocavity
idea: A 3 nm gold nanoparticle sits in a 7 nm sealed cavity between two electrodes, held against either wall by van der Waals adhesion (~2 eV, ~80 kT from the Hamaker estimate). A charge-plus-field pulse throws it across in ~100 ps, and the read senses tunneling current, which changes ~1e4x with particle position.
why: A rigid-body position bit has no leakage tail (fact 3), an exponentially sensitive non-destructive read (fact 8), and a cell volume of ~10 nm3.

title: Vacuum-gap tunneling floating node: oxide-free, wear-free charge storage
idea: Separate a floating metal node from its write electrode by a 2-2.5 nm vacuum gap, made by ashing a sacrificial ALD carbon layer in O2 plasma at <=250 C. Write by direct or field-emission tunneling through vacuum (~ns at 2-3 V); retention is set by gap width because tunneling is exponential in it (2.5 nm gives >1 s).
why: Oxide wear-out needs a lattice to damage and vacuum has none, so this targets unlimited endurance for a floating-node store. No capacitor pillar (fact 1), and the cell stacks in BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric delivers planar 11,000-electron bits
idea: Sputter Al0.7Sc0.3N at <=400 C, thinned to ~5 nm to keep coercive voltage near 2 V. Its 2Pr ~ 200 uC/cm2 delivers ~1.8 fC (~11,000 e) from a flat 30x30 nm capacitor, versus ~0.1 fC from a dielectric, in a 1T1C destructive-read cell with no high-AR pillar.
why: Polarization charge density, not k*E, breaks the charge wall (fact 1) and removes the 60-75:1 etch. Endurance (1e6-1e8 today) is the key risk, to fix by electrode and strain engineering.

title: Built-in-bias antiferroelectric ZrO2 minor-loop dynamic polarization cell
idea: ALD ZrO2 crystallizes antiferroelectric at <=350 C. Asymmetric TiN/RuO2 electrodes (~0.5 eV work-function offset) shift the double loop so zero bias sits inside one lobe, and the field-induced ferroelectric state stores the '1', relaxing over a designed ~1 s with no wake-up or imprint fatigue.
why: 2-3x the charge per area of a linear dielectric (fact 1) with antiferroelectric endurance >1e12. A refreshable volatile ferroic store at BEOL temperature.

title: Tungsten-free BiSb topological spin-Hall write line for nanomagnet bits
idea: Write perpendicular nanomagnets with a BiSb topological-insulator line (spin Hall angle ~10) sputtered at <=250 C after the 350 C MTJ anneal, instead of W/Ta/Pt. The large spin Hall angle cuts the required current density ~10x.
why: ~10x lower SOT write energy and no tungsten (China ~80% chokepoint), in a fully BEOL-stackable magnetic bit.

title: Self-dissolving silver nanocluster bit with designed one-second lifetime
idea: In an RT-sputtered SiOxNy:Ag diffusive layer, a write pulse nucleates a sub-2 nm Ag bridge that conducts ~uA. Gibbs-Thomson surface energy then dissolves it with tau set by cluster size and matrix diffusivity, designed at ~1 s, and refresh rewrites it.
why: Dissolution kinetics replace capacitor leakage as the retention clock, with a uA gain-like read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1). Avoids permanent oxygen-vacancy damage, targeting 1e10+ endurance versus ReRAM's ~1e6.

title: Ultra-wide-gap amorphous Ga2O3 storage node holding 0.1 fF for hours
idea: Generation leakage scales as ni ~ exp(-Eg/2kT), so moving from IGZO (3.2 eV) to RT-sputtered a-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) cuts intrinsic generation by ~1e13. A 0.1 fF planar MIM node behind an a-Ga2O3 access device then holds a 0.3 V signal for >1e4 s, read by a local gain transistor.
why: Shrinks the capacitor ~50x (fact 1) and removes refresh (fact 3) in a planar BEOL-stackable cell, going beyond the IGZO prior work. The risk is defect-limited (not intrinsic) leakage in amorphous films.

title: ALD oxide quantum-well charge bucket gated by band bending
idea: Grow a 3 nm In2O3 well between Ga2O3 barriers (dEc ~ 0.9 eV) by ALD at <=300 C, under a gate and over a read channel. A gate pulse bends the bands to inject electrons thermionically, retention tau = tau0*exp(dEc/kT) gives ~0.5 s at 85 C, and stored electrons shift the read channel's threshold.
why: Retention is set by a band offset chosen by composition, not by a leakage tail (fact 3), with no capacitor (fact 1). Capacitorless and repeatable in many BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Redox-molecule monolayer: quantized one-electron-per-molecule pseudocapacitive storage
idea: Line a shallow 20 nm x 200 nm hole (10:1 AR) with a room-temperature self-assembled monolayer of ferrocene/porphyrin redox molecules on short conjugated linkers (~1e14 per cm2), with a solid polymer electrolyte supplying counter-ions. Each molecule stores exactly one electron at a fixed Nernstian potential, ~12,000 e per cell, sensed as a potential step.
why: Faradaic charge per area beats dielectric charge, so a 10:1 well matches a 70:1 pillar (fact 1). Electron transfer must reach >1e8 per second.

title: Spin-crossover molecular film switched electrically between spin states
idea: Sublime a ~10 nm Fe(II) spin-crossover film (triazole or bispyrazolylborate family) at <=200 C. Cooperative lattice strain gives a ~20 K-wide room-temperature hysteresis between low-spin and high-spin; field or charge-injection pulses switch it, and a vertical junction reads the 10-100x conductance or dielectric contrast.
why: A molecular-scale bistability set by lattice elasticity, with no charge to leak (fact 3). Uses abundant iron and organics and is compatible with top tiers.

title: Order-disorder molecular-rotor ferroelectric printed below 150 C
idea: Print a molecular ferroelectric (diisopropylammonium bromide or imidazolium perchlorate class, Pr 10-20 uC/cm2, Tc >400 K) as the final tier. Polarization comes from whole cationic dipoles rotating in place rather than ions hopping through vacancies, and ~1 V pulses write it.
why: Rotation should avoid vacancy-driven fatigue (endurance) and gives ~10x a linear dielectric's charge per area (fact 1), processed at <=150 C from earth-abundant C/H/N/Br.

title: Selector-only chalcogenide: threshold-voltage polarity stores the bit
idea: A single RT-sputtered GeAsSe ovonic threshold switch is both selector and memory. A write pulse of one polarity shifts its threshold voltage by ~1 V through field-driven defect and ion redistribution without crystallizing, and the read uses the opposite polarity.
why: Removes the separate storage layer, giving a one-layer 4F2 cross-point stackable at <=350 C, with no melt (energy, endurance beyond PCM) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Nanoconfined monatomic antimony phase-change cell that cannot segregate
idea: Fill 5 nm TiN-lined pores with pure Sb by RT sputtering; confinement stabilizes the amorphous phase, and melt-quench of ~100 nm3 costs ~10 fJ. A single element cannot phase-separate, which removes the composition drift that kills Ge-Sb-Te endurance.
why: Attacks PCM's endurance failure mode at its root (no elemental migration), with fJ writes in a stackable cross-point (density).

title: Proton-intercalation channel bit using the lightest mobile ion
idea: Stack a BEOL (<=350 C) WO3 channel over a hydrogenated HfO2 or PSG proton reservoir. A ~10 ns gate pulse moves ~1e3 protons into the channel and shifts conductance ~10x, read non-destructively; protons are chosen because ionic mobility scales inversely with ion mass and size.
why: Ionic storage at near-electronic speed with a uA read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1). The risk is retention and endurance under ns pulses.

title: Strain-switched magnetostrictive nanomagnet driven by sputtered piezo AlScN
idea: A sputtered AlScN piezo layer strains an elliptical FeGa nanomagnet, rotating its easy axis 90 degrees between two states that an MTJ reads. Write energy is the piezo's CV2 at 0.3-0.5 V (~1 aJ), with no current through the magnet and every film deposited at <=350 C.
why: ~100x below STT write energy (fact 10), with Galfenol avoiding rare earths and Pt, in a BEOL-stackable cell.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal at 400 C erasing the leakage tail
idea: The <=13 fA retention-tail cells come from trap-assisted tunneling through a few interface and junction dangling bonds. A 20 atm D2 anneal at 400 C passivates them, and the Si-D bond resists hot-carrier and field depassivation several times better than Si-H, cutting the tail at its physical source.
why: Pushing the tail out 10x stretches refresh intervals 2-4x, saving ~50-75% of refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) with one anneal step that fits existing fabs.

title: Tier-for-litho: 64 BEOL tiers on DUV beat EUV density
idea: Bits/area = tiers / cell area. Pattern a <=400 C capacitorless cell at 4F2 with F = 45 nm on immersion DUV (no EUV), deposit 64 monolithic tiers as a blanket stack, and cut them with one 3D-NAND-style high-AR etch, reaching ~127 nm2/bit versus ~864 nm2 for 6F2 at 12 nm.
why: Removes EUV (fact 4) and much of the 55% depreciation burden. Thermal budget is what blocks monolithic stacking, and the 400 C limit is exactly what unlocks it.

title: License a BEOL memory tier into existing U.S. logic interconnect lines
idea: Package a <=400 C storage element as a foundry PDK option: 2-4 memory tiers inserted between upper metal layers on logic wafers already running in Arizona, Oregon and New York, built with the existing ALD/PVD/etch tools. The foundry earns revenue per wafer on bits added above the logic die.
why: Turns idle BEOL capacity into memory supply without a $15B DRAM fab (capital), puts memory on-die to cut data movement (fact 5), and raises U.S. manufacturability.

title: Panel-scale memory on Gen-8.5 glass using nanoimprint
idea: Because nothing exceeds 400 C, build a planar oxide or ferroic storage array on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass in display-type panel lines, patterned by roll-to-plate nanoimprint at ~30 nm with ~4 stacked tiers. Each panel has ~78x the area of a 300 mm wafer.
why: Panel cost per m2 is ~10-20x below wafer cost, attacking capital intensity and cost per bit. Panel lines can be built in the U.S. faster than DRAM fabs.

title: Negative-U oxygen-vacancy metastability as an electrically-written bit
idea: In RT-sputtered amorphous ZnSnO or InGaZnO, oxygen vacancies are negative-U: ionized VO2+ relaxes the lattice outward, and a configuration-coordinate barrier (~0.5-1 eV) blocks recapture. Hole injection writes (vacancies ionize and the channel conducts), electron injection with gate field erases, and the read senses channel conductance.
why: Turns the defect behind oxide-TFT persistent photoconductivity into the storage element, with no capacitor (fact 1). Retention is set by a lattice-relaxation barrier, not a junction leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Electrostatic pull-in hysteresis latch held at zero static current
idea: A sputtered TiAl nanobeam over a dielectric-capped electrode is bistable at any hold voltage between its release and pull-in voltages. A small up or down pulse sets the state, the capacitive hold draws no DC current, and the read senses the ~2x capacitance change; process is <=400 C BEOL MEMS.
why: Static storage held by electrostatics, with no leakage-driven refresh (fact 3), no capacitor charge requirement (fact 1) and no ohmic contact to wear. Dielectric charging and stiction are the risks.

title: Freestanding SrTiO3 membrane transfer gives k~300 capacitors cold
idea: Grow single-crystal SrTiO3 on a donor wafer over a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, release it in water, and transfer and bond the ~5 nm membrane onto the memory wafer at <=300 C. Crystallization happens off-wafer, so the product never exceeds 400 C yet gets a k~300 dielectric.
why: k~300 beats the k~70 that fact 1 requires, allowing 5 fF at AR ~15:1 or as a planar 3D tier. The constraint is met by moving heat off the product wafer; dead-layer k loss is the risk.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly carving sub-10 nm storage islands without EUV
idea: Anneal a high-chi block copolymer (e.g., PS-b-PDMS) at <=250 C so it self-assembles into hexagonal 8-10 nm-pitch dots registered to a coarse DUV guide pattern. Transfer the dots as hard masks that define magnetic, ferroic or charge-storage islands; pitch comes from chi*N thermodynamics, not photon wavelength.
why: Sub-10 nm bit definition with no EUV (fact 4), raising density for many BEOL storage elements.

title: On-die microheaters re-anneal worn cells every few hours at 350 C
idea: Embed a TiN heater serpentine under each memory mat. After ~1e10 cycles, migrate the mat's data and pulse it to ~350 C for ~10 ms to anneal out generated traps, vacancy clusters, ferroelectric imprint and MTJ barrier defects; the temperature stays inside the BEOL budget, so it heals without damage.
why: Converts finite-endurance elements (ferroelectric, ReRAM, charge-trap at 1e8-1e11 cycles) into effectively unlimited endurance, making them DRAM-class. Heater-based self-healing has been shown for NAND.
